neet_phy_u07_t05_1.working: In streamline (steady) flow, the velocity at a given point stays constant in time. Streamlines never cross, and the flow has no eddies.

neet_phy_u07_t05_3.working: Re = ρvD/η = 1000 × 0.2 × 0.02 / 1e-3 = 4000. Since Re > 3000, the flow is turbulent.

neet_phy_u07_t05_4.working: Reynolds number is the ratio of inertial to viscous force (A-III). Critical velocity is the speed beyond which flow turns turbulent (B-IV). Continuity expresses mass conservation (C-II). Crowded streamlines mark higher speed (D-I).

neet_phy_u07_t05_5.working: Critical velocity vc = Re·η/(ρD). A is true (vc rises with η). B is false (vc falls with D). C is true (Re is dimensionless). D is true (Av is constant). E is false (vc falls with ρ).
